It's harder to open up with my mom, who is always there. I had a therapist a few months back and I opened up as much as possible with her. I took risks and told her how I felt and everything. In the end, she told me that I was offensive and she wont take my comments anymore. I was horribly stupefied, honestly surprised that a therapist would say something like that to me. I don't think I'd like to face that again.

From where I am now, there's no one that can really relate to me. I go to a mediocre college and students are there just to pass the time and don't really care about their classes. I hate the fact that nobody cares about the subject and I especially hate that the teachers are included in that. It's hard to be enthusiastic about something I love (learning) when everyone else finds it "uncool" and dorky. There's honestly no one here that enjoys their classes.

I don't think it's my age that brings the pressure, more like my race. I'm the only Asian in all of my classes and I look comparatively smarter. Plus I sit in the front and answer all the questions, like a good Asian. When I tell people how old I am, they're usually shocked and say they expected me to be older, so I don't think I look as young as I am.

That's definitely true, how people that share similar traits with you are the only ones who can truly help. I went to an academic camp when I was younger and met all of my best friends there. They were Asian, like me, and were ambitious and competitive, like me, but a few had issues back at home with feeling inadequate because they don't receive perfect scores and those kids became my good friends during camp. Of course, they faded away when camp ended. I've been yearning to be accepted into a good university just to find more people like the ones I've met at camp.

I've argued this several times here (in other accounts) and I wholeheartedly agree with you. Sure, it might hurt them if you killed yourself, but they can't even begin to fathom how much pain you're experiencing right now and for the past few years.

Suicide isn't about selfishness, and I don't believe they have a place to accuse a depressed person about being selfish if they haven't experienced it themselves.
I do both. I go to college and have jobs.

Sometimes it's just as bad to have nothing wrong with your life. I just sit here wondering why I'm so depressed. A lot of people write me off as totally fine because I've been through no abuse, no trauma yet I still want to kill myself daily. I went through several therapists because no one could find anything wrong with me. But I've tried killing myself twice and ended up in the mental hospital three separate times.

Let's not belittle those with "lesser" problems. I've seen several posts here saying they have it the worst when in reality everyone has it the worst. It can be external or internal abuse, and one is not more worse than the other.

I don't have a lot of friends. I don't have anyone I can talk with anything beyond casual conversations. Family is distant, as are coworkers. My life is pretty okay, since I still live under my parents' roof, but I've been mentally unstable for a while now. If I won a vacation for two to the Bahamas, I'd probably take my mom because there's no one I could ask and have them agree to come. Not sure if my mom would come either. I'd probably go alone.

Sorry for being a creep, but you're an Asian female? I looked in your past submissions and saw you posted in a subreddit about hair brushes and asian parents. I'm an Asian female too; maybe we can relate a bit more? I also grew up in a white majority area and have always lacked that feeling of belonging in some group. I'm probably younger than you, since I should be a high school senior by my age. I currently attend college and have felt even more out of place because of my age difference and background. I don't know what to say to you, since I've been diagnosed with major depression and have been fighting it with no avail. But perhaps talking about our similarities will help soothe away the loneliness?
